audit.why: 56.27% over 391 games against a chart that concedes level 1 and level 6 to Mel and gives Camille everything else. A strongly favoured melee-into-immobile-mage lane with two ranged-poke stages carved out is coherent, so no stage moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her spikes carry no cooldowns at all, which matters more here than usual because Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s - by far the longest basic ability in the lane. 'Wait out her reflect' with a 38s number attached is a completely different instruction from 'wait out her reflect'.
audit.why: Cooldowns from champ-data/_kits/mel.json: Radiant Volley 10/9/8/7/6s, Rebuttal 38/35/33/29/26s, Solar Snare 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Golden Eclipse 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: mid, late and wants.foe[1] now carry Rebuttal's 38s at rank 1 and Solar Snare's 11s, so the bait-and-commit advice has a real clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Her reflect is attributed to her R in five places. Rebuttal is her W: it prevents her taking damage and reflects projectiles. Golden Eclipse (R) is something else entirely and far more dangerous to a diver - it strikes every enemy marked with Overwhelm at ANY distance on the map, scaling with stacks, so her ult is a global threshold finisher rather than a defensive reflect. 'Her W/E zone' is also wrong: W is the barrier, the zone is Solar Snare (E). Camille's Hookshot is called a stun; Riot's text says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Rebuttal: 'Mel forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage.' Golden Eclipse: 'Mel strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her, dealing additional damage for each stack of Overwhelm.' Searing Brilliance applies Overwhelm on any ability or attack damage. _missing-interactions.json flags execute-threshold for this pairing.
audit.corrected: spikes[1..2], mid, late, whys[4], whys[6], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] now name Rebuttal as the barrier to wait out and Golden Eclipse as a global Overwhelm detonation you track by stacks, not by distance.

edits.before: This is your window. Hold E and bait her ranged Q, then E-in, slash the outer edge of W across her for the max-HP chunk and the heal, and double-Q through her. Her R reflects incoming damage and projectiles, so don't dump your full combo into it blind — wait it out, then she's a squishy mage with no melee answer. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum leaps her into the arena and switches off the one thing she's good at: range. Save the E leap to dodge her snare or sidestep her W/E zone mid-fight, then finish her.
edits.after: This is your window. Hold E and bait Radiant Volley, then E-in, slash the outer edge of W across her for the max-HP chunk and the heal, and double-Q through her. Rebuttal (W) stops her taking damage entirely, so don't dump your combo into it blind — wait it out, and at rank 1 it is 38s before she gets another. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum leaps her into the arena and switches off the one thing she's good at: range. Save the E leap to dodge Solar Snare, then finish her.

edits.before: You own the straight 1v1 all game — your true-damage Q2 and W max-HP slash carve through her squishy AP build, and R drags her out of any teamfight for an isolated kill. The only real risk is letting the game drag: at two-plus items a fed Mel bursts you from range before your E connects, and a well-timed R reflect can flip an over-committed dive. Close the lane, snowball your side-lane pressure, and never E into her without your Q and W ready to follow — pick her off the moment she steps up to poke.

edits.before: Mel pokes from range with her Q and you have no gap-closer until level 2, so don't walk into her auto-Q range to land a melee Q — last-hit from the edge, let your passive shield eat one magic hit, and accept a little chip. Once you hit level 2 the lane flips hard: E grapples the wall behind her and dashes in for the stun, then the empowered Q recast lands the true-damage burst. She has no dash, no point-blank peel beyond her W/E zone, and a squishy body, so every time your Hookshot is up she has to play for her life.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Mel steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. notes: Mel's reflect is her W (Rebuttal), not her R, and the matchup gets it wrong five times. That misattribution also buried the thing a diver most needs to know: Golden Eclipse strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy REGARDLESS OF DISTANCE, so walking away from a fight at low HP is not safety - the number to track is your Overwhelm stack count, not the gap. 'Her W/E zone' compounded it by treating the barrier and Solar Snare as one thing. Rebuttal's 38s at rank 1 is the single most useful cooldown in this lane and appeared nowhere. mel.json flags Searing Brilliance as an autoReset; Riot's text describes bonus projectiles on her next attack after an ability, so I wrote neither claim rather than assert a reset the description does not support.
